Coal India Posts 57% Profit Surge in Q2 on Higher Offtake and Improved Pricing

31 Oct 2026, 09:20 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.thehindu.com

Financial Performance Overview

Coal India Ltd reported a 57% year-on-year increase in net profit, reaching ₹6,547 crore for the second quarter. The state-owned miner's financial growth was primarily supported by stronger fuel offtake and better price realisations, which successfully outweighed rising input costs.

Alongside the earnings report, the Kolkata-headquartered company declared a second interim dividend of ₹10.25 per equity share.

Operational Drivers and Production Figures

During the quarter ended September, coal offtake rose 12% year-on-year to 186.34 million tonnes (MT), bolstered largely by sustained power demand. Average price realisations across fuel supply agreements, e-auctions, washed coal, and other categories increased by 7% to ₹2,346.21 per tonne.

However, overall production grew by a more modest 4% year-on-year to 151.37 MT, missing the company's internal target of 157.83 MT for the period.

Revenue and Rising Expenses

Revenue from the sale of products advanced 21% year-on-year to ₹43,724 crore, while total revenue also climbed 21% to reach ₹44,179 crore.

At the same time, expenditure grew. The company's cost of materials—incorporating expenses on explosives, oil and lubricants, heavy earth-moving machinery, spares, and timber—increased 20% year-on-year to ₹2,752 crore.

Practical Implications and Analysis

What Is Confirmed

  • Net profit rose by 57% year-on-year to ₹6,547 crore.
  • A second interim dividend of ₹10.25 per share was announced.
  • Offtake increased 12% to 186.34 MT, and average price realization rose 7% to ₹2,346.21 per tonne.
  • Total revenue grew 21% to ₹44,179 crore, while material costs increased 20% to ₹2,752 crore.

What Remains Unknown

  • Specific future production targets and whether quarterly shortfalls will impact annual output goals.
  • Future trajectories for e-auction premiums and specific sector-wise demand shifts beyond the power sector.

How to Verify

Readers can review the official financial disclosures and reports published by Coal India Ltd or read the original coverage on The Hindu.
